I don't want to spread malware that doesn't affect me to other people who might still be using Windows XP, an abacus, or other rudimentary stuff like that.
What antivirus software would you recomend?

Your best bet is to learn how to use a computer without contracting malware.

Using Linux is a big step, because it is not targetet by most malware/virus/hacker developers. Basicly, never install anything you're not sure is safe. Linux has the added security of you using a standard User account, while services and vital systems run on completely separate privilege levels and userspaces. This means, that if something is compromised, i.e. lets say someone finds a vulnerability in your system and if they could exploit it, they would still only have limited access, usually just write access in the folder of said service. This is something Unix/Linux systems have been doing for ages, and windows has taken a long time to get to. Linux Malware on Wikipedia has some pointers and a more in-depth explanation of why linux is more secure, and what you should be looking out for.

Basicly, most Linux software comes from software repositories, and they are kept clean by maintainers, so they are safe. The dodgy areas are browser plugins, or stuff you download from independent developers, but again these are run under standard-user privileges and can't do system wide infections.

A Computer is a tool, the more you know the better you can protect yourself:)

ClamAV is the standard antivirus scanner to catch windows viruses that you might accidentally share from your Linux host. I believe you can even set up inotify to have ClamAV scan each file after it has been uploaded.

To protect against Linux specific threats, you'll want to periodically run RKhunter and/or chkrootkit.

I also highly recommend using SELinux and IPtables to further lock down your Linux system.
